messages:
jordan: Customer reported invoice INV-2026-0424-1102 with ~11.8k unexpected completion tokens. They were on mobile and using the JS SDK streaming resume flow with prefill_on_resume=true. Happened 2026-04-24 ~18:23 UTC. @li @sam can you triage? :eyes:

li: Can you paste the minimal repro + request_id? Also confirm whether they included the system message on each resume and which SDK version.

jordan: request_id: r-9c8a7b. Minimal repro curl below — they explicitly set prefill_on_resume:true and resend the messages array on resume:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"stream_session_id":"sess-99","seq":7,"resume":true,"prefill_on_resume":true,"messages":[{"role":"system","content":"Assistant: follow safety rules"},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize this text"}]}'
```

jordan: Client-side estimator (SDK) logs show: prompt_tokens=22 completion_est=28. Billing shows ~11,840 completion tokens billed across many resume events.

sam: Billing tie: r-9c8a7b appears in the metering window you mentioned. Invoice lines show many small completion chunks that sum to the delta. Did the customer see duplicate outputs in the UI?

jordan: Customer says UI looked normal (no visible duplicates). They suspect invisible server-side fragments being re-applied on resume that the SDK estimator doesn\'t count.

vela: Infra capture for sess-99 shows we reapply session_prefill when resume=true and we currently re-run postrun hooks during resume. Excerpt from metering trace:

2026-04-24T18:23:01Z INFO metering event request_id=r-9c8a7b emit_id=em-001 chunk_kind=prompt tokens=22
2026-04-24T18:23:02Z INFO metering event request_id=r-9c8a7b emit_id=em-002 chunk_kind=completion tokens=496 postrun_tag=hook_v3
2026-04-24T18:23:03Z INFO metering event request_id=r-9c8a7b emit_id=em-003 chunk_kind=completion tokens=496 postrun_tag=hook_v3

vela: The repeated completion token events correspond to postrun tool/KV output fragments that are invisible to the client UI but are emitted server-side on resume. The SDK estimator currently ignores postrun/tool tokens, so local estimates are much lower.

li: Hypothesis: on resume we re-run postrun hooks and re-materialize invisible fragments without emitting stable idempotency metadata, so metering treats each emit as billable distinct content. Need to verify if emit_id or postrun_hash is stable across replays.

jordan: I reproduced locally with a short script: start stream with a system prefill, drop the network after first completion chunk, then resume by resending the same messages + prefill_on_resume=true. Metering shows duplicate postrun emissions; SDK estimate remains small.

li: Short-term mitigation idea: collapse metering events by stream_session_id + postrun_hash for the invoice window to avoid double-billing identical postrun fragments. Medium-term: runtime should attach an idempotency_token to postrun emissions so metering can dedupe in real-time. Proposed pseudocode for middleware:

```
// if resume and fingerprints match, mark emission to skip metering
if (resume && fingerprint(messages) == session.last_prefill_fingerprint) {
  emission.meta.skip_metering = true
}
```

sam: Don\'t issue credits yet. I\'ll place invoice INV-2026-0424-1102 on hold pending audit logs. We need an audit trail before we adjust billing.

vela: Action items: vela -> run dedupe query across the last 48h and return list of affected request_ids; li -> PR to set skip_metering flag for resumed identical prefill emissions; jordan -> collect raw stream capture from the customer (client-side logs + server raw stream) and upload to secure link; sam -> open dispute hold and compute tentative credit estimate.

metering-bot: Automated detection: repeated postrun emissions for request_id=r-9c8a7b across stream_session_id=sess-99; flagged for manual review.

jordan: Thanks all 0 I\'ll loop the customer in once we have audit traces and will share reproducible script. :lock:
